findings: Push past 30. The RL bot almost never stays while its bust chance is under 15% (1% of the time at most). Staying only becomes more likely than hitting at about a 24% bust chance, which is about 34–38 points. It busts in 42–46% of its rounds, against 33–39% for SmartBot's careful play, and still wins more: in a race to 200, big rounds matter more than safe ones.

Let the scoreboard set your risk. 100+ points behind the leading rival, it keeps hitting until about 46 points. Level, about 35. 100+ ahead, it banks at about 23. SmartBot's stay point hardly moves (25–29).

Flip Four and Just One More are weapons, never self-help. It uses them on itself in under 1% of cases (SmartBot: 91% and 54%), and aims them at the leader 70% of the time, where a random opponent would be 44%.

÷2 goes to the leader, not the biggest hand. 63% of ÷2 cards go to the player with the highest total. SmartBot gives it to the biggest current hand (87% of the time), which is the leader only 45% of the time.

Minus cards are already paid for (Brutal Mode). A bust keeps your minus cards, so they count whether you stay or bust: hitting only risks your number cards. The bot plays it that way. Holding minus cards it stays at a lower round score (about 34 vs 37 points) but at a slightly higher bust chance (27% vs 25%).

Go for the seventh card. Holding six different numbers it hits 87% of the time, and still 66% of the time at a 40–50% bust risk: Flip 7 is worth +15 and ends the round before rivals can catch up. It Flips 7 about twice as often as SmartBot (2.7–3.7% vs 1.3–1.6% of rounds).

+15 when ahead, −15 only to slow a runaway leader. After a Flip 7 it takes the +15 93% of the time. It never chooses −15 while leading, but does so 10% of the time while trailing, aimed at the leader 84% of the time. The more players, the less −15 is worth (4–6% at 4–6 players vs 21% one-on-one), because it only hurts one of several rivals.

Don't pay the Shakedown. Offered the choice between paying a rival 10 points and taking a card, it pays under 1% of the time. Even at a 30–40% bust chance it pays only 3% of the time. Paying moves 10 points to a rival for sure; a card that doesn't bust it adds to its own round. SmartBot, which works the odds out card by card, comes to the same answer: it pays under 1% of the time.

Special Delivery: a bust for a rival, or a gift to itself. When the flipped number can bust someone, it delivers the bust 74% of the time, and 57% of the cards it hands to rivals go to the leader (a random rival would be 39%). A number that can't bust anyone it keeps 56% of the time, and it keeps 70% of the actions and 82% of the keepers.
